title: Operator Precedence and Expression Grouping
learningObjectives: Explain the key idea in operator precedence and expression grouping.
Identify the relevant syntax and rules.
Trace each example and predict the result.
Apply the concept in a small program.
Avoid a common mistake related to this topic.

understand.concept: Operator precedence determines how operators are grouped in an expression when parentheses are absent. Associativity determines grouping among operators of the same precedence. Parentheses are the clearest way to express intended order.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding expression grouping avoids logic and calculation bugs and makes code easier to review.
understand.analogy: Think of this as a control or calculation rule that tells a program how to handle a particular situation consistently.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a starting point; C++ syntax, types and execution rules determine actual behaviour.
understand.explain:
## Precedence
Multiplication and division bind more tightly than addition and subtraction. Comparisons and logical operators have their own precedence levels.

## Associativity
Associativity resolves grouping for operators with equal precedence, such as chained arithmetic or assignment.

## Best practice
Do not memorize precedence as a substitute for readable code. Add parentheses for non-obvious expressions and avoid mixing assignment, comparisons and logical operators in one dense line.
